policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Angola tourist-visa exemption
policies.summary: Presidential Decree 189/23 expressly lists 98 beneficiary countries. Ninety-six map to this repository’s passport catalog; Cook Islands and Niue have no separate codes in that catalog. A later official MIREX notice reports approval of an amendment for the Philippines, but no official Gazette promulgation or effective date was recovered, so it is not promoted here.
conditions: Up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per calendar year.
Passport validity of more than six months and, where needed, an international vaccination certificate remain required.
This policy does not establish work, study, medical-treatment, residence, business-specific, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual admissibility treatment.

conflicts.explanation: Presidential Decree 189/23 expressly lists Samoa among the tourist-visa-exempt countries; the current official 98-country confirmations show the regime remains in place.

unresolved.reason: A live official MIREX mission notice reports Council of Ministers approval of an instrument adding the Philippines to the tourist-visa-exemption regime (https://arabiasaudita.mirex.gov.ao/web/noticias/conselho-de-ministros-aprova-ajuste-das-pensoes-do-ministerio-do-interior), but no official Gazette promulgation or entry-into-force date was recovered. Approval alone is insufficient to classify the current nationality-wide baseline; all other ordinary-passport routes remain unresolved.

The current official sources reaffirm the 98-country tourist exemption but do not establish a current nationality-specific ordinary-passport rule for this code outside that explicit list. Generic consular tourism-visa services and online processing do not safely establish a nationality-wide eVisa, visa-on-arrival or advance-visa classification; bilateral, document and case-specific exceptions remain unresolved.
